title: Evaluation transpose at common finite coefficient stages
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite $E\subset\Omega$ put $B_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $E_T=B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$, and $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ valued in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal C_E(T)=D^b_c(T,E)$ for the raw rationalization of derived-complete integral constructible complexes, with its specified completed finite scalar transitions $S_{F/E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the common-stage pair category of these $\mathcal C_E(T)$, with Hom groups the directed colimits over common finite fields [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $A=E_T,R_T$, let $\mathcal D_T(A)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of bounded objects whose cohomology sheaves have a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which they are pro-etale locally finite free over $A$.

Use the tensor, internal Hom and evaluation of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $M,N\in\mathcal C_T$ be a permitted Hom pair: at some common finite field they have integral constructible representatives whose completed internal Hom is constructible, and $H\in\mathcal C_T$ is the coefficient-passage internal Hom, transported at larger fields by the specified rational Hom scalar comparisons. Denote its right evaluation by $e:H\otimes M\to N$, using the signed symmetry to convert the left-evaluation convention when necessary.

For every $L\in\mathcal C_T$, the evaluation map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_T}(L,H)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_T}(L\otimes M,N),\qquad a\longmapsto e\circ(a\otimes1_M)$$
is a bijection natural in $L$ and in the permitted pair. It is the directed colimit of the finite rational completed tensor-Hom transpose bijections; for every finite extension, extending a pairing and then transposing equals extending its transpose followed by the specified rational Hom comparison, for arbitrary constructible target. These assertions include all localized arrows and the signed swap. Only a finite stage witnessing the permitted Hom pair is required; there is no site-perfectness hypothesis on $M$.

source.place: BS Lemma 3.4.11, with raw rationalization and common-field descent; old step 9; HRS: literature/hemo-richarz-scholbach-constructible-sheaves_arXiv-2305.18131.pdf; precise map normalization is the agent-written argument retained in report.md.

proof.text: For the witness-domain equivalence, a permitted compositum pair is itself a finite-field witness. In the reverse direction use integral_constructible_internalHom: every pair of integral constructible objects on this separated finite-type scheme has constructible ambient Hom. Translate the intrinsic sfIntegralConstructible predicate to and from boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral with sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy, retaining the same finite reductions and interval. Apply this to the entries extended to their compositum. This proves the required predicate without choosing a witness or assuming perfectness.

Take S from podCommonClosed_existsUnique, obtaining its exact finite-stage normalization. For each a:L→H(P), apply injectivity of S.transpose to prove S.transpose.symm(a)=T(a,1)≫ev_P: parameter naturality reduces its transpose to a followed by transpose(ev_P)=a. This identifies the evaluation map with the inverse additive equivalence, so it is bijective.

For f:L′→L and g:P→Q, use normalized common evaluation naturality for g and precompose with T(f≫a,1). Functoriality of T identifies the two composites with the required inverse-transpose naturality equation, using the evaluation formula just proved. For the signed-swap equation apply common tensor braiding naturality to (1_M,a), and postcompose with ev_P.

For every finite coefficient embedding E→F apply rationalHomScalar_transpose D l hl X E F to obtain both the exact displayed scalar-transpose square and its signed-swap clause, for all rational arrows and arbitrary permitted targets.

proof_origin.place: Stage-3 Lean assembly from the existing normalized common closed datum, integral Hom closure, evaluation naturality and braiding naturality; finite scalar clauses use rationalHomScalar_transpose.
